patch_description: The current ansatz uses only a phase-type (CRZ) entangling layer shared via a single parameter "ent". This limits the entangling operation to diagonal (Z-basis) correlations, missing amplitude-mixing (X-basis) correlations that could help separate harder-to-classify groups. I add a parallel CRX layer immediately after the existing CRZ entangler, on the same disjoint pairs (0,1),(2,3),(4,5),(6,7), sharing a single new parameter "crx_ent". This is a minimal addition (+1 distinct parameter, +4 gates, +1 depth) that introduces non-diagonal two-qubit rotations, increasing the expressive power of the entangling block without significantly increasing overfitting risk, since the parameter is fully shared. This should help boost the worst-group margin (the dominant score term) by giving the circuit richer entangling structure to fit hard-to-separate samples, while keeping the parameter count increase minimal.
